related_questions.question: Can excess HSA contributions be removed without penalty?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, excess HSA contributions can be removed without penalty if withdrawn by the tax filing deadline (including extensions) for the year the contributions were made. If the excess contributions and any associated earnings are withdrawn before this deadline, they are not considered part of the taxable income for that year and no excise tax is applied.

list.title: Penalty-Free Removal:
list.snippet: The key is to withdraw the excess contributions (and any earnings those contributions generated) by the due date of your federal income tax return, including extensions.

list.title: Tax Implications:
list.snippet: If you withdraw the excess contributions and earnings before the tax deadline, you don't owe the 6% excise tax on those excess contributions. However, the earnings on the excess contributions are still considered taxable income for that year and should be reported as "Other Income".

list.title: Form 5329:
list.snippet: You will likely need to file Form 5329, "Additional Taxes on Qualified Plans (Including IRAs) and Other Tax-Favored Accounts," to report the excess contribution removal and the associated earnings.

list.title: Consult with your HSA provider:
list.snippet: It's best to work with your HSA provider to ensure a smooth withdrawal process and to understand the specific steps required to correct the excess contribution.

list.title: Form 1099-SA:
list.snippet: Your HSA provider will also report the excess contribution removal on Form 1099-SA, " Distributions From an HSA, Archer MSA, or Medicare Advantage MSA".

list.title: What if you miss the deadline?
list.snippet: If you miss the deadline for withdrawing the excess contributions, you will be subject to the 6% excise tax on the excess amount for that year and any subsequent years the excess remains in the account.
